alt: The Cascade Lounge — Styles flow. Ideas spill. A warm green lounge with a coffee mug, amber lamp, CSS book, and orange chair.
prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: finished homepage social-share / Open Graph card for The Cascade Lounge, a CSS publication. Wide landscape composition intended for 1200 by 630 pixels (approximately 1.9:1).

Input image 1: edit target and background. Preserve its recognizable forest-green lounge, soft window light, amber ribbed lamp, speckled cream coffee mug, CSS book, marble table, green plant, framed retro art, and burnt-orange chair. Keep the lounge still life on the right and clean dark-green negative space on the left. Recompose/crop the scene gracefully into a wider social-card layout, retaining its refined photorealistic material texture and warm light.
Input image 2: branding and typography reference ONLY. Do not reproduce its website interface or page layout.

Create one polished, evergreen branded share card, not a screenshot. Put the large headline in the left half with elegant Newsreader-like editorial serif typography: "The Cascade" on one line in warm cream, and "Lounge" directly below in generous burnt-orange italic serif lettering. This is the dominant title and must be perfectly readable at social-preview size. Above it, use the brand's simple four rounded vertical bars in olive, orange, cream-gold and orange, with a small, widely spaced cream sans-serif caption "THE CSS LOUNGE". Below the headline, set the exact tagline "Styles flow. Ideas spill." in warm cream. Along the lower left, set "Articles · Quick Wins · Resources", then the small clear domain "thecascadelounge.com". Use only these exact words and the existing "CSS" on the book; no invented words.
Keep ALL words comfortably inside an 8% inset safe area. Maintain generous negative space, disciplined hierarchy, crisp text, strong contrast, and the original forest/cream/amber/burnt-orange palette. No extra objects, people, border, browser chrome, navbar, buttons, article title, date, labels, watermark, or competing graphics. Keep the right-hand scene prominent and visually continuous with the left background.
